'''''Euryops chrysanthemoides''''' (with the common names '''African bush daisy''' or '''bull's-eye''') is a small shrub native to [[Southern Africa]] that is also grown as a horticultural specimen in [[Tropics|tropical]] to [[Subtropics|subtropical]] regions around the world.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gilman |first=Edward F. |author2=Linda Landrum |title=''Gamolepis chrysanthemoides'' Fact Sheet FPS-220 |url=http://hort.ifas.ufl.edu/shrubs/GAMCHRA.PDF |publisher=University of Florida Cooperative Extension Service Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences |date=October 1999 |accessdate=2008-06-22 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20060524014206/http://hort.ifas.ufl.edu/shrubs/GAMCHRA.PDF |archivedate=May 24, 2006 }}</ref>  



==Description==
[[File:Margaritón - Margarita amarilla (Euryops chrysanthemoides) - Flickr - Alejandro Bayer (7).jpg|thumb|left|Detail of ''Euryops chrysanthemoides'' flower]]
It is a compact, densely branched, leafy, evergreen shrub, 0.5 to 2m in height. The leaf surface is smooth and green. The species was moved to ''Euryops'' from the genus ''Gamolepis'' on the basis of chromosome counts.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Ornduff|first=Robert|author2=Peter H. Raven|author3=Donald W. Kyhos|author4=A. R. Kruckeberg|title=Chromosome Numbers in Compositae. III. Senecioneae|journal=American Journal of Botany|volume=50|issue=2|date=February 1963|pages=131–139|doi=10.2307/2439846|publisher=American Journal of Botany, Vol. 50, No. 2|jstor=2439846}}</ref>  

==Distribution==
''Euryops chrysanthemoides'' is indigenous to [[southern Africa]], where it occurs in the [[Eastern Cape]], along the coast and inland, to [[KwaZulu-Natal]], [[Mpumalanga]] and [[Eswatini]]. It is usually found on forest edges, in riverine bush and in ravines, as well as in coastal scrub, grassland and disturbed areas. 
It is a ruderal weed in [[New South Wales]], although it is not invasive in all places where it is cultivated or has naturalized.<ref>{{cite book|last=Harden|first=Gwen J.|author2=editor|title=Flora of New South Wales|year=1993|publisher=University of New South Wales Press|isbn=0-86840-172-2}}</ref>
